title: Learning from Ukraine's unrivaled experience of Russian cyber warfare
gist: Ukraine now records far more Russian cyber attacks but suffers far less damage (critical/high incidents fell from 1,048 to 59 between 2022 and 2024 while attacks nearly doubled); the author argues Western institutions should treat Ukrainian data as a real-time detection resource and let Ukraine design multilateral cyber exercises.

insights.claim: Registered Russian cyber attacks on Ukraine nearly doubled from 2,194 in 2022 to 4,315 in 2024, while critical or high-severity incidents fell from 1,048 to 59.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Evidence that sustained defensive investment sharply cuts impact — a benchmark for cyber-defense ROI.
insights.locator: Over four years later, Ukraine now registers

insights.claim: In the early weeks of the 2022 invasion a Ukrainian SOC team handled fourteen to twenty cases daily, a volume a French counterpart assumed was weekly.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Illustrates the scale gap between wartime and peacetime threat environments.
insights.locator: This was the reality of Ukraine’s cyber defenses

insights.claim: Russian cyber operations against Ukraine often reappear elsewhere, run in parallel, or spill over into the wider Euro-Atlantic area, especially nearby EU states, per researchers such as Eduard Chornyi at SET University.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Ukrainian threat intel is a leading indicator for attacks on European firms.

insights.claim: A joint Western advisory in April 2026 described Russian military intelligence targeting Western logistics and technology companies supporting Ukraine, likely including compromise of internet-connected cameras near border crossings, military sites and rail stations in Ukraine and neighboring NATO states.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Logistics and tech vendors supporting Ukraine are active targets — elevated cyber risk and insurance exposure.

insights.claim: Organizations can be seriously damaged by cyber attacks even when not the original target, so they must map everything they depend on digitally, not only what they own.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Third-party/supply-chain cyber risk management is a growing spending category.

insights.claim: Most Western institutions are set up to receive briefings rather than coordinate responses in real time, a structural gap rather than a knowledge gap, compounded by underfunding and staff shortages in critical-infrastructure cyber coordination.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Real-time threat-sharing platforms and critical-infrastructure cyber staffing are under-served markets.
insights.quote: which makes this a structural gap rather than a knowledge issue
insights.locator: In order to address international threats

insights.claim: Ukrainian data should be treated as a detection resource rather than a news story, feeding continuously into detection systems instead of annual briefings.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Threat-intel vendors integrating Ukrainian telemetry may have an edge.
insights.quote: it is crucial to treat Ukrainian data as a detection resource and not a news story

insights.claim: Ukraine has participated in many Western cyber exercises but has never been invited to set the scenario; the author argues it should design and lead multilateral exercises.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Opportunity for Ukrainian cyber firms in training and exercise services.

insights.claim: Ukrainian cybersecurity companies have spent years converting Russian attack experience into training material, and the State Service of Special Communications and Ministry of Digital Transformation launched the CISO Campus platform for cyber leaders.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Ukraine's cyber sector is maturing into an exportable services industry.
insights.locator: Ukraine is already building its own training

insights.claim: Joint training, shared incident analysis and applied research exchange between Ukrainian and Western institutions are not happening at a scale matching the threat.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Gap signals under-investment in Western cyber preparedness against Russian tactics.
